newsitem.title: GERMANY: Martinair to lift German/Swiss cargo rates Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Martinair to lift German/Swiss cargo rates Oct 1.

text.p: Dutch airline Martinair said it would raise air cargo rates from Germany and Switzerland by five to 10 percent to nearly all destinations from October 1.
This would equate to 20-30 pfennigs a kg in Germany or 16-25 centimes a kg in Switzerland.
"We believe the market will grow rapidly through the good export situation and the strong dollar," Heiner Sass, the carrier's central Europe cargo director, said.
Dutch market rates were also likely to be upped to reflect the higher German rates although no final decision had yet been taken, he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Rates from France and Italy would probably be increased by a similar amount from October 15.
Frankfurt-based Sass, responsible for Germany, France, Switzerland and Italy, said the German price hike was generated by a booming exports market.
"We think there will be a 'hot autumn' and we could even have problems to offer space to all those who want it. This could continue into 1998 for some destinations," Sass added.
Martinair had seen very strong summer cargo sales in Germany and had generated a good cargo load factor, he noted. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
